# NoID Privacy for Linux

> NoID Privacy for Linux is a Bash hardening-posture audit for Linux desktops. It emits host-adaptive findings across 42 fixed-weight security and privacy sections and is non-remediating by default. Explicit RPM-baseline, AIDE-live, and NoID-image policy-refresh opt-ins write only their documented state/log files. Invoked system services may keep normal operational logs. The `--ai` flag emits a structured remediation prompt; model suggestions remain untrusted until reviewed.

It focuses on desktop privacy surfaces (browser policy, app telemetry, DNS/VPN observations, webcam/Bluetooth, MAC randomization, session lock, and keyrings) in addition to kernel, firewall, SSH, encryption, MAC, package, and service hardening. It reports a section-weighted posture score and separate assessed-weight coverage. Neither value is a compliance result, compromise probability, or proof of a clean host.

## Facts

- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
- Language: Bash 4.3+; common OS utilities are capability-detected and optional-tool absence can reduce evidence
- Non-remediating by default: no intentional configuration changes or package-metadata refresh. No telemetry or report upload. Documented active probes contact third parties by default; `--offline` is equivalent to `--skip interfaces --skip netleaks`, suppresses every audit-generated network probe, and retains local VPN assessment. No VPN is valid and informational by itself.
- Distros/desktops: exact validation depth is recorded in `Docs/SUPPORT.md`; parser recognition alone is not a support claim
- Exit codes: 0 = no FAIL/WARN, 1 = FAIL present, 2 = WARN-only, 130/143 = interrupted
- Output modes: human-readable, `--json` (CI), `--ai` (remediation prompt), CIS RHEL 9 / DISA STIG coverage mapping (`--cis-l1`/`--cis-l2`/`--stig`)
